correctness.rationale: Explicit ring multiplication and units yield the exact vertex set. For u!=0, nondegeneracy gives exactly q^n annihilator elements in the maximal ideal. Excluding zero and, when B(u,u)=0, the vertex itself yields all three degrees. Isotropic counts follow from Gauss sums or a Frobenius-semilinear functional. Highest-degree multiplicity q-1 identifies q, vertex count identifies n, the lower-degree multiplicity identifies isotropy. Complete finite-field classification of symmetric forms then gives similarity and an explicit algebra isomorphism. The coefficient-field lift provides the general equicharacteristic scope. The executable enumerates and checks 109 examples; the infinite claim rests on proof.

originality.rationale: The source-to-claim implication comparison does not locate an existing theorem that the simple zero-divisor graph's degree multiset determines the ring isomorphism class for all equicharacteristic short finite Gorenstein algebras with one-dimensional radical square, across odd and even fields. Kadu's Proposition 3.6 supplies the orthogonality reduction, and classical symmetric-form classification is acknowledged. The complete three-stratum degree distribution and degree-only ring reconstruction are the claim. Publication priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: A broader theorem asserting graph-degree recoverability for finite local rings or orthogonality graphs may cover this specialization without the same terminology.
Some primary texts were inspected by relevant statements and sections, not page-by-page exhaustively; publication priority requires independent literature validation.

value.rationale: Recovering the isomorphism class of a finite local algebra from the simple zero-divisor graph's coarse degree multiset is a canonical structural question. The theorem gives a complete if-and-only-if classification for the infinite Gorenstein Hilbert-function (1,n,1) family, distinguishes both even-dimensional types in odd and even characteristic and sharply states where the invariant applies. It is not merely a restatement of quadratic-form counting; the graph-to-ring reconstruction is the application.
